text: Krylov eigenvalue solvers Krylov eigensolvers approximate a few eigenpairs through a small subspace instead of diagonalizing a large matrix in full. Arnoldi, symmetric Lanczos and shift-invert require different assumptions. Problem and representative equations Build Kₘ(A,v)=span{v,Av,…,Aᵐ⁻¹v}. Arnoldi gives an orthonormal Vₘ and upper-Hessenberg Hₘ. Solve Hₘy=θy and set x=Vₘy. The last Arnoldi vector and hₘ₊₁,ₘ give the Ritz residual. Algorithm Expand the basis using matrix-vector products and orthogonalization, solve the projected eigenproblem and restart when needed. Hermitian matrices permit a Lanczos three-term recurrence. Shift-invert targets interior eigenvalues but each inverse action requires a linear solve. Conditions and pitfalls Finite-precision loss of orthogonality can create ghost duplicates. For nonnormal matrices, a small residual need not imply a comparably small eigenvalue error. State B and the inner product in generalized problems Ax=λBx, and assess inner-solve tolerances for shift-invert. A small eigen-residual supplies backward-error information about an eigenpair of a nearby matrix; it need not imply small eigenvalue or eigenvector forward error for a nonnormal matrix. Individual-vector matching can be unstable in a close cluster, where principal angles between invariant subspaces can be more appropriate. What to check Check scaled residuals ∥Ax−θx∥/(∥A∥+|θ|), orthogonality, known eigenpairs and clustered/repeated eigenvalues. For symmetric cases compare Rayleigh quotients, and record restarts and initial-vector sensitivity. The added release separates eigenvalue spacing from nonnormality on small matrices and compares eigenvalue/subspace errors with independent references as Krylov dimension and residual vary. Passing a residual check alone is not presented as an accurate true eigenvalue. Report conditioning alongside measured errors in clustered and nonnormal controls; no guarantee for arbitrary large nonsymmetric systems is implied. Projected solves and dense references may share LAPACK infrastructure and are not described as fully independent backends. Analytic eigenvalues and constructed pseudoeigenpair controls provide additional checks. Unrestarted small-matrix educational examples with separated extreme eigenpairs. Interior/clustered eigenvalues, very large sparse matrices, strong nonnormality, shift-invert and implicitly restarted Arnoldi are outside scope. A small eigenpair residual alone is not treated as a rigorous eigenvalue-error bound for nonnormal matrices.
